mechanism: Both drugs inhibit CYP3A4 and can prolong QT interval; ranolazine is metabolized by CYP3A4 and chloroquine is a potent CYP3A4 inhibitor, leading to increased ranolazine levels and additive cardiac risk.
action: Monitor ECG and QTc interval closely; consider dose adjustment of ranolazine or alternative antimalarial; baseline and periodic cardiac assessment recommended.
